skill.name: improve-codebase-architecture
skill.description: Reviews a codebase for shallow modules, weak interfaces, scattered decisions, and refactoring opportunities using CONTEXT.md and ADRs.
skill.summary: Finds architecture deepening opportunities that improve testability, locality, and AI navigation.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution and path-traversal alerts are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and relative documentation links. No malicious shell execution, network access, credential access, or prompt injection was found. The remaining concern is low-risk repository exploration and documentation edits that users should review.

remediation.issue: Repository exploration may read broad project context.
remediation.suggestion: Limit exploration to relevant directories when the user names a feature area, and avoid reading secrets or generated artifacts.

remediation.issue: The workflow can create or update CONTEXT.md and ADR documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before making documentation edits, and show a diff before applying changes.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Repository Access and Documentation Writes
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to read project context, walk the codebase with an Explore subagent, and update CONTEXT.md or offer ADR creation. This is legitimate for architecture review, but it can expose repository contents to the agent and create documentation changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly direct repository reading and conditional documentation edits. The behavior is expected for the skill, so the concern is operational rather than malicious.

content.value_statement: Architecture reviews often miss shallow modules, scattered decisions, and weak test surfaces. This skill guides AI agents to find practical refactoring opportunities using project language.
actual_capabilities: Reads CONTEXT.md and ADR files before recommending architecture changes.
Identifies shallow modules, weak interfaces, coupling, and poor locality.
Presents numbered deepening opportunities with files, problems, solutions, and benefits.
Uses defined architecture terms for modules, interfaces, seams, adapters, depth, leverage, and locality.
Guides follow-up discussion before proposing concrete interfaces.
Compares alternative interface designs after a candidate is selected.
limitations: It needs repository access to inspect relevant files and documentation.
It does not prove that a refactor is worth the delivery cost.
It needs human judgment when recommendations conflict with existing ADRs.
It focuses on architecture and testability, not performance profiling or security auditing.

use_cases.title: Refactor a tangled feature area
use_cases.description: Find modules where complexity is spread across callers and propose a deeper module shape.

use_cases.title: Prepare for AI-assisted maintenance
use_cases.description: Improve naming, locality, and test surfaces so future agents can navigate the code more reliably.

use_cases.title: Review architecture before major work
use_cases.description: Use domain context and ADRs to identify seams that should change before implementation begins.

prompt_templates.title: Find architecture friction
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a repository or feature area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the improve-codebase-architecture skill to review this repository. Start with CONTEXT.md and ADRs, then list the strongest deepening opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Review one feature area
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for a known problem area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the improve-codebase-architecture skill on the checkout flow. Identify shallow modules, weak seams, and tests that would improve after refactoring.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize refactor candidates
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review across several possible changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to compare deepening opportunities in this module cluster. Rank them by locality, leverage, implementation risk, and test impact.

prompt_templates.title: Design alternative interfaces
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced follow-up after choosing a candidate.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the interface design workflow for the selected candidate. Generate several different interface options, compare trade-offs, and recommend one.

output_examples.input: Review the billing area for architecture problems.
output: A numbered list of deepening opportunities in billing modules.
Each candidate includes affected files, the problem, the proposed direction, and testability benefits.
A question asking which candidate should be explored next.

output_examples.input: We selected the order intake candidate. Help shape the interface.
output: A short framing of constraints and dependencies.
Several alternative interface designs with different trade-offs.
A recommendation based on depth, locality, seam placement, and test surface.

output_examples.input: Our ADRs reject a repository pattern, but the current design is painful.
output: A focused review of the ADR conflict and current architectural friction.
A recommendation on whether the decision is worth reopening.
Optional wording for an ADR update if the user chooses to record it.

best_practices: Run it on a focused feature area when the repository is large.
Keep CONTEXT.md and ADRs current before asking for recommendations.
Review proposed documentation edits before accepting them.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a substitute for product or domain decisions.
Do not add a seam only because it makes mocking easier.
Do not ask for concrete interfaces before choosing a refactor candidate.

faq.question: What kind of codebase is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is best for repositories where architecture, testing, or module structure is becoming hard to reason about.

faq.question: Does it change code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on analysis and discussion. It may propose documentation edits when the workflow calls for them.

faq.question: Does it require CONTEXT.md?
faq.answer: No. The skill reads CONTEXT.md when present and proceeds silently when it is missing.

faq.question: How does it use ADRs?
faq.answer: It reads ADRs to avoid reopening settled decisions unless current friction makes a decision worth revisiting.

faq.question: Can it design new interfaces?
faq.answer: Yes. After a candidate is selected, it compares several interface options and recommends one.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that can inspect repository files.
